brief: Morgan Stanley initiates thematic coverage of digital assets with a base case it calls convergence: public protocols add permissioning while institutions adopt public rails where distribution and liquidity matter. Four developments drive the timing. Regulation defines a compliant path through the GENIUS Act, stablecoin supply exceeds $300bn, exchanges extend operating hours, and crypto-native firms move inside the regulatory perimeter. About a quarter of Bloomberg World Financials Index members by count and 60% by market cap have live, piloted or announced digital-asset initiatives. The note separates two questions: whether the technology is adopted and who captures the economics. Value can accrue to incumbents that keep the client relationship, to crypto-native equity, or to tokens, and to tokens only where the structure creates durable demand net of issuance. Bitcoin is treated separately on a monetary digital-gold thesis, at about 5% of above-ground gold, with a five-year base case of a mainstream satellite allocation of 1-4% for retail. Crypto prices sit 37% below the October 2025 peak despite adoption progress, because marginal demand still comes from retail, leverage and narratives.
